newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks firmer, seen stagnating.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks firmer, seen stagnating.

text.p: Croatian stocks held their ground with slight new gains in slow trade on Wednesday, but market participants foresaw a period of stagnation setting in.
"By the end of the week prices will remain more or less where they are and we might even see some correction," said an analyst at consultancy and brokerage I.F.C.
Six of 11 active stocks rose, two fell and three were flat. Volume shrank to 12,018 units and turnover to five million kuna from almost 21 million on Tuesday.
Food concern Podravka was the most actively traded issue with 8,977 shares sold. It edged down seven kuna to 368 after peaking at 390 earlier in the day.
"Podravka is now stabilising and chances are it may edge down, although it remains very much traded," said the analyst.
Leading gainer was Zagrebacka Banka's E-series preference stock, up 5.26 percent to 1,000 kuna on volume of 583 units.
Zagrebacka's fully-listed ordinary shares closed 60 kuna or 3.24 percent higher at 1,910 kuna. But volume was negligible which traders said might indicate a correction on the cards.
The other blue chip, drugs firm Pliva, added two percent to 510 kuna and traded 94 shares. Still it was seen as the most stable stock in the long term.
Chocolate maker Kras firmed 10 kuna or 2.17 percent to 470 kuna with 578 shares changing hands.
Hoteliers traded mixed with Jadranturist and Laguna continuing to rise to 330 and 1,415 kuna respectively.
Istraturist was flat at 200 kuna while Riviera led decliners, dipping 23 kuna or 13.93 percent to 142.
The second tarnche of public debt refinancing bonds (JDB) rose to 8.90 percent above par from 8.45 a fortnight ago.
